question: Should OpenClaw accept a fixed 64 KiB and 250 ms limit for the legacy Urbit response-consumption compatibility path, after current-head live authentication proof?
rationale: The prior implementation intentionally consumed the full response for deployments that finalize cookies after body consumption, so selecting a shorter finite boundary is an upgrade-compatibility decision rather than a result unit tests can settle.

options.title: Require current-head live compatibility proof
options.body: Obtain redacted authentication evidence from a representative Tlon/Urbit deployment on the current head, then merge if the fixed bounds are acceptable.

options.title: Accept the bounded failure mode explicitly
options.body: Merge with the stated 64 KiB and 250 ms limits while accepting that unusually slow legacy cookie-finalization flows may need a follow-up.

options.title: Pause for a different compatibility design
options.body: Hold the PR if no representative deployment can validate whether a fixed global deadline is safe for supported Urbit installations.

recommendation.title: Require current-head live compatibility proof
recommendation.body: Obtain redacted authentication evidence from a representative Tlon/Urbit deployment on the current head, then merge if the fixed bounds are acceptable.
